chapter: Moving to California and the war years
title: Deciding to go to the Coast in 1940
summary: He had long wanted to go to California, quit the Spirits, played in Atlanta and took the $40 freighter to San Pedro.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I told you I was with Ben Burnie?
Yeah, I was just trying to think about that whole period in there, different people that you -- the Spirits, you say you quit the Spirits though for a while there.
Yeah.
Around '38, something like that.
I quit the Spirits around then.
Because you got disgusted.
Yeah.
But then you reformed -- you came out
to the Coast.
I came out to the Coast.
When did you get that idea?
I had it in my mind all the time when I was hearing so much about it, you know.
Uh-huh.
I was hearing so much about coming out to the Coast. And then people would tell me, 'Why, you'd be something else out there on the Coast. Why don't you try to get out there?'
Uh-huh.
So that was my ambition. To get out to the Coast.
But you finally made up your mind around-- it was 1940, right?
Yeah.
Was it just like you just thought about it and thought about it and then finally you just decided that now's the time?
I'd been thinking about it, you know. I had it on my mind to go to the Coast, because I'd be hearing so much about what was happening out here.
Yeah.
So I just made up my mind I'd come out here.
So, as you recall then, you went down
to Georgia for about a month.
Atlanta, Georgia.
Yeah. And you had that gig down there for about a month, got stuck there.
Yeah, I got stranded down there.
And then you took the boat.
I took the boat.
How much did it cost? It must not have cost much to get on that freighter.
Yeah. I remember that. But I sure hated to give up that $40.00.
Where did you stay on the boat? Was it with the seamen or was there some cabins there, or --
There were some cabins there.
Yeah. And you came into San Pedro?
San Pedro.
Do you remember that?
Yeah.
